analysis_notes.note_on_eitza_edge_888: The eitza edge (המקבל עצה מחכמי הדור → המתקת הדינים) encodes the central causal argument of the Torah: receiving wise counsel PRODUCES the sweetening of dinim. This is the eitza flow BETWEEN Package 1 (dinim) and its resolution. The המתקת הדינים node is the bridge concept that sits at the boundary — it is the outcome that Package 1 and Package 2 together produce, driven by the Tzaddik's chesed illuminating the contracted intellect.
analysis_notes.note_on_torah_structure: Torah #143 is an extremely concise Torah (4 sentences). Its bechina graph is sparse (3 edges, 5 nodes, 2 components) because most of the teaching is expressed through eitza (causal) logic rather than bechina (shared-nature) identifications. The fundamental argument is: [not-knowing = tzimtzum = dinim] --eitza--> [receiving-counsel] --eitza--> [המתקת הדינים], with the bechina of [wise-counsel = illumination = chasadim] being the mechanism of the eitza. This is a structurally clean teaching: two poles (contraction/dinim vs. expansion/chasadim) connected by the act of receiving counsel.
